The Opportunity:
Maitland City Council's Pathways program is a fantastic way to kick-start your career and gain professional experience in local government!
Commencing in January 2027, for a period of two years, we have two exciting opportunities for Graduate Civil Engineers to join our organisation.
In this role, you will undertake a graduate program developed specifically for you, giving you exposure to a range of civil engineering functions for the investigation and delivery of civil and recreation infrastructure projects undertaken by Council. These duties are going to help you develop a solid foundation to your civil engineering career.
About you:
To be successful in this role you will possess:
- Degree level qualifications in Civil engineering in the previous two years or completion of degree by January 2027
- Contemporary industry knowledge of civil engineering areas
- Experience and understanding in project support and the research, analysis and presentation of information
- Current Class C driver's licence
Benefits:
This Graduate position is temporary full time (two-year contract) with a commencing salary of $1,414.58 weekly, plus 12% superannuation. Graduates will also have access to Council's great staff benefits including:
- Flexible work arrangements
- One extra week of "My Leave" a year (to use how you like!)
- Ongoing training and development
- Fitness Passport
- Healthy Employee Program
To apply:
To apply for this opportunity, please click 'Apply Now' and submit your resume and cover letter.
Questions:
To viw the role charter click 'Apply Now'. If after reading the role charter you have any questions, please contact the recruitment team at Recruitment@maitland.nsw.gov.au
More information regarding Council's Pathways Program can be viewed via https://www.maitland.nsw.gov.au/pathways-program.
Applications close: Sunday 25th October 2027
Only candidates with current Australian work rights (Australian citizens, permanent residents, NZ citizens with a current passport, valid work visa) will be considered.
What happens next?
Once applications close, we will review all candidates' details against the role requirements and will be back in touch with you to advise the status of your application.
Please note, prior to an offer of employment being made, recommended candidates will be required to undertake a medical assessment (including drug and alcohol testing). Council also completes a range of other pre-employment checks which may include reference checks, psychometric testing or a criminal history check. For more information about the recruitment process, visit the "Jobs at Council" page on our website.
Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
Maitland City Council is dedicated to providing a workplace that is inclusive and supportive and is reflective of the diverse community we serve. We support equal opportunities for all employees, and encourage applications from people from all cultures, nationalities, identities, and abilities. The Opportunity
Our client who is a first class civil engineering consultancy who is seeking a Graduate Civil Engineer to join their experienced Cairns-based engineering team.
This is an opportunity to apply your technical skills to projects that have a genuine impact, from roads that connect communities and drainage systems that protect property, through to bridges, culverts, water infrastructure and land development projects.
This consultancy provides civil engineering and project management services across government, private development, infrastructure and regional projects throughout Far North Queensland and beyond. Their project portfolio includes roads and drainage, water and wastewater infrastructure, subdivisions, bridge and crossing works, airports and major infrastructure projects.
The Role
You will be a hands-on member of the engineering team, contributing to the planning, design and delivery of a broad range of civil infrastructure projects.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Developing practical and cost-effective civil infrastructure designs
- Supporting road, drainage, stormwater, water and land development projects
- Preparing technical drawings, documentation and engineering reports
- Assisting with project delivery and undertaking site inspections
- Monitoring construction outcomes, quality and project requirements
- Identifying technical issues and developing practical solutions
- Supporting approvals, compliance and stakeholder requirements
- Liaising professionally with clients, contractors and project stakeholders
- Working closely with senior engineers while developing your technical capability

You will be a motivated Civil Engineer who enjoys civil design, practical problem solving and wants exposure to a diverse range of projects.
You will ideally have:
- Degree qualification in Civil Engineering
- Practical experience in civil design is a must
- Exposure to roads, drainage, stormwater, water, subdivisions or similar projects

- Good attention to detail and an ability to manage competing priorities
- Clear written and verbal communication skills

Job Offer
- $75,000 - $85,000 + super, negotiable based on experience
- Relocation assistance available
- Diverse civil projects from concept and design through to construction
- Exposure to roads, drainage, water, infrastructure and land development
- Hands-on project and site experience
- Mentoring from experienced senior engineers

- Opportunity to contribute ideas and influence project outcomes

- Long-term career stability and genuine project variety
How To Apply
To build your career with a company that values quality engineering, practical solutions and the work you deliver, please click Apply and please include any civil design experience you have undertaken in your application.
About Us
With Head Office in Cairns and offices in Townsville and Brisbane. We specialise in professional, administration, engineering and industrial recruitment, permanent and temporary placements for both commercial and government enterprise. We are proud to connect great people with meaningful careers.

Build More. Build Your Career.
Ready to kick-start your engineering career on some of Southeast Queensland’s most exciting infrastructure projects?
Seymour Whyte's Graduate Program gives ambitious engineering graduates the opportunity to work on major projects, take on real responsibility from day one, and develop the technical, commercial and leadership skills needed for a successful career in construction.
Through our structured two-year development program, you'll gain hands-on experience across major civil infrastructure projects, work alongside industry leaders, receive dedicated mentoring and build the skills and confidence to accelerate your career.  You'll be trusted with real responsibility, supported to grow and given the opportunity to make a genuine impact while helping deliver infrastructure that connects communities.
About the Project
We have an exciting opportunity for a Graduate Civil Engineer to join our Beerburrum to Nambour (B2N) Rail Upgrade project.
This a major infrastructure project transforming the North Coast Line on the Sunshine Coast. The project includes rail duplication, new and upgraded transport infrastructure, improved road overpasses and enhanced signalling systems, all aimed at increasing capacity and reliability across the network. Once complete, B2N will deliver faster and more efficient travel while improving connections between the Sunshine Coast, Moreton Bay and Brisbane, creating lasting benefits for local communities and the region.
Why Join Seymour Whyte?
At Seymour Whyte, we believe the best way to learn is by doing. Our structured Graduate Development Program is designed to fast-track your career through hands-on project experience, mentoring from industry leaders and tailored professional development opportunities.
From day one, you'll be embedded in a live project team, contributing to the delivery of major infrastructure projects that shape communities across Australia. You'll gain exposure to a range of disciplines, build your technical and commercial acumen and develop the confidence to take ownership of meaningful work early in your career.
Throughout the program, you'll be supported by experienced mentors, participate in structured development workshops, and connect with a national network of graduates and professionals who are invested in your success.
What's in it for you?
- Work on a landmark civil infrastructure project from day one
- Gain exposure to multiple disciplines across project delivery
- Receive structured mentoring, coaching and development support
- Learn from experienced industry leaders and subject matter experts
- Build a strong professional network across projects and regions
- Be part of a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture
- Access career opportunities within the VINCI Group, a global leader in construction, infrastructure and concessions
Whether your passion lies in construction delivery, engineering, project management or leadership, our Graduate Development Program will provide the foundation, support and opportunities to help you build a rewarding and long-term career with Seymour Whyte.
To learn more about our Graduate Program, click here.
About You
You're in your final year of a Bachelor of Civil Engineering and ready to turn everything you've learned into real-world experience on major infrastructure projects.
Whether you've gained experience through an internship, vacation work, industry placement or part-time employment, you're eager to learn, build your skills and make a meaningful contribution from day one.
We're looking for graduates who are curious, motivated and excited about a career in civil construction.
You'll bring:
- Final-year studies in a Bachelor of Civil Engineering
- Practical experience through internships, vacation programs, placements or other employment
- A genuine passion for civil construction and infrastructure projects
- A positive attitude and willingness to learn from experienced industry professionals
- Strong communication and teamwork skills
- A commitment to safety, collaboration and creating a positive team culture
- Flexibility to travel or relocate as opportunities arise throughout your career
Most importantly, you're ready to take the next step, embrace new challenges and build a rewarding career delivering projects that make a lasting impact on communities across Australia.
Seymour Whyte Benefits
- Employee recognition and awards that celebrate contribution and achievement
- An employee share program, providing the opportunity to invest in the long-term success of the business
- Birthday leave, because celebrating life's milestones matters
- The option to purchase additional leave to support travel, study or personal commitments
- Fitness and wellbeing discounts through WHEREFIT (gym memberships, meal plans and fitness brands)
- Travel, retail, lifestyle and wellness discounts
- Workplace banking benefits and everyday financial savings through CommBank and Flare
Seymour Whyte is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds, including veterans.
Our commitment to an equitable construction industry extends to an inclusive culture that embraces our differences and gives everyone the opportunity to grow and be equally valued. We're unified in our direction toward having a workplace that is balanced and fair for all.
Next Steps:
- Submit your CV online to apply for this role
- All successful applicants will be required to undergo a pre-employment medical and criminal history check
- Applications will only be accepted from candidates who have the right to work in Australia
To learn more about us, visit www.seymourwhyte.com.au

candidates.content_text:
City of Armadale
Armadale, Perth WA
Engineering – Civil/Structural Engineering 
$102,000–$117,000 per annum plus superannuation
Shape a growing City’s infrastructure. Plan capital projects through design, costing and approvals, with WFH and flexi-time for a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Shape infrastructure projects across asset renewal, upgrades and growth.
 -  Flexible working with WFH and accrued flexi-time towards a 9-day fortnight.
 -  Superannuation up to 15%, subject to conditions, plus free gym membership.
 Help shape the projects that shape our City
Good infrastructure starts with good decisions. Understanding what is needed, testing the options and resolving the detail before construction begins.
At the City of Armadale, you’ll help make those decisions. As one of Western Australia’s fastest-growing local governments, we’re planning new infrastructure while improving and renewing the assets our community already relies on.
We’re looking for a Project Planning Engineer who brings practical judgement, asks good questions and takes pride in preparing projects properly.
If you’re enjoying your current role but would welcome the opportunity to influence a growing City’s infrastructure, this could be your next move.
Why Armadale?
Our Strategic Community Plan sets a clear direction: facilities that meet community needs, better public places, and infrastructure that is functional, inclusive and sustainable.
You’ll help turn those priorities into practical projects, balancing technical requirements, cost, risk and long-term asset performance. Across renewal, upgrade and growth projects, you’ll tackle varied challenges and see how your work contributes to the community.
You’ll also have flexibility in how you work, including working from home and the ability to accrue flexi-time to work a nine-day fortnight, with arrangements agreed around role and team requirements.
Your role
Working in our Asset Planning team, reporting to the Project Planning Lead, you’ll progress identified infrastructure priorities into well-defined, costed and approved capital projects ready for delivery.
Starting with Project Initiation Documents developed by Strategic Asset Management, you’ll coordinate investigations and detailed designs, refine cost estimates and progress the approvals needed for capital works program entry.
You’ll work with engineering and landscape design specialists, consultants, asset operators and delivery teams to:
 - Develop clear project scopes, specifications and budget requirements.
 - Coordinate investigations, technical advice and detailed design activities.
 - Prepare and refine cost estimates, checking assumptions, contingencies and constructability.
 - Progress approvals, utility clearances, statutory consents and other project requirements.
 - Prepare complete project packages for review under the City’s Project Management Framework.
 - Resolve risks and gaps early, considering procurement, construction sequencing and handover requirements.
Your work will help the City make informed investment decisions and give delivery teams confidence in each project’s scope, cost and readiness.
What you’ll bring
You know what it takes to prepare an infrastructure project for delivery. You can work through technical detail, challenge assumptions constructively and bring the right people together to resolve issues.
We’re looking for:
 - Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering, Project Management, Construction Management or a closely related discipline**, or equivalent demonstrated experience in project planning and infrastructure development.
 - Experience planning civil infrastructure or construction projects.
 - Sound knowledge of cost estimation, contingency allowances and key cost drivers.
 - The ability to coordinate technical input across disciplines and progress third-party approvals.
 - Familiarity with project management frameworks and project approval requirements.
Flexibility and benefits
 - Working-from-home arrangements and flexi-time, including the ability to accrue time towards a nine-day fortnight.
 - Superannuation contributions of up to 15%, subject to employee contributions and applicable conditions.
 - Free Armadale Fitness and Aquatic Centre membership**, including the gym, pools, sauna and group fitness classes.
 - Wellbeing activities throughout the year.
 - Novated leasing opportunities.
Our values—Care; Are Better, Together; Learn & Grow; and Seize Today, Shape Tomorrow—guide how we work. We listen, share knowledge and welcome people who bring ideas and take responsibility for their work.
Interested? Let’s talk
You don’t need to be actively looking for a new job to explore this opportunity.
For an initial confidential conversation, contact People Services on 9394 5189 or hr@armadale.wa.gov.au. 
Ready to apply? Submit your CV and a brief cover letter through the application link, outlining your relevant experience and interest in the role.
We review applications as they are received and may close the advertisement early.
*The City of Armadale welcomes applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disability, people from culturally diverse backgrounds and people of all genders and identities.*
*We are committed to child safety and recruitment practices that support a safe and inclusive community.*

- Roads and highways
- Civil infrastructure
- Renewable energy projects
- Drainage and earthworks
- Buildings and associated civil works
- Temporary and permanent works

- Managing project documentation and workflows in ProjectWise
- Coordinating drawing production across multidisciplinary teams
- Assisting with document control and drawing management
- Leading CAD standards, drafting efficiency and quality processes
- Exploring and implementing AI tools to improve drafting productivity, consistency and quality
- Structural drafting where required

Essential
- Strong experience using Bentley MicroStation and/or OpenRoads Designer
- Strong experience using and managing ProjectWise
- Experience drafting civil infrastructure projects in Victoria, particularly on major projects
- Excellent attention to detail and drawing presentation
- Strong understanding of engineering documentation standards
- Ability to work collaboratively within a project team
- Strong communication and organisational skills
Desirable
- Experience with OpenRoads Designer
- Experience with renewable energy projects
- Structural drafting experience
- Interest in automation, digital engineering and AI tools
- Experience working in ISO-aligned quality environments
- Experience in training and managing other drafters
Why Join Hullcon?
- Work directly with senior engineers and project leaders
- Exposure to major transport and renewable energy projects
- Genuine opportunity to shape how AI is used within engineering design
- Diverse project portfolio with technical challenges and variety
- Collaborative, office-based environment focused on mentoring and development
- Growing consultancy with significant opportunities for career progression
- Competitive salary package based on experience
Apply
If you're a skilled MicroStation Draftsperson looking to work on meaningful projects and are excited by the future of AI-enabled engineering design, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role
We are seeking a talented Project Engineer (Civil/Structural) to join our team at FGI Developments in Cairns, QLD. This is a full-time position that offers a fantastic opportunity to work on diverse and challenging infrastructure projects in the tropical north. As a Project Engineer, you will play a crucial role in the planning, design, and delivery of civil and structural engineering projects, working closely with project managers, clients, and site teams to ensure projects are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest standards. This role is based across our Cairns sites, providing you with the opportunity to work on regionally significant infrastructure while maintaining a strong connection to the local community. Note this is not a FIFO role.
Key responsibilities
- Plan and schedule work to minimise impacts to stakeholders
- Control all engineering activities and processes on projects
- Ensure quality, cost, safety, performance and time schedules are met
- Interface with procurement, operations, commercial, quality, and expedite logistic functions to ensure the project schedule is adhered to

- A degree in an engineering discipline that is accredited by Engineers Australia. Note: Transcripts will be required for Interview.
- A minimum of 5 years post qualification experience
- Demonstrated ability to plan and organise schedules and resources
- Experience with defence, civil or road infrastructure projects
- Excellent English communication skills, with the ability to negotiate and influence
- An understanding of cost control
- Experience in Quality Assurance
- Experience with Microsoft Project and other MS programs
- Experience with Auto Cad
- Must be able to read and interpret drawings and have a technical view of civil and mining projects
- Must be fit for work
- Must be able to pass a National Criminal History Check

- Must pass a medical and drug test
Benefits
- Competitive remuneration package
- Opportunities to work on exciting projects
- Diverse opportunities to grow
- Ongoing training for career progression
- Supportive team environment
About us
FGI is an Australian owned and operated civil construction, bulk earthworks and agriculture company — developed to the regional demands of civil, mining and agricultural developers across Australia. We offer a complete package of skills and resources to deliver projects in civil construction, bulk earthworks, road construction, drainage, concrete and water infrastructure.

The City of Canada Bay is a thriving, colourful community, surrounded by the beautiful bays of Sydney Harbour. The area is also known for its parklands, cycle paths and walkways. City of Canada Bay Council’s values underpin how we operate: 
We act with integrity| We empower our people| We are respectful| We work together| We innovate.
Help shape the infrastructure that supports our community
We are seeking an enthusiastic and capable Infrastructure Engineer to join our team and contribute to the planning, design and delivery of infrastructure projects that support our growing community.
This is an opportunity to apply your engineering expertise across a diverse range of infrastructure projects, from initial investigations and design through to construction, project delivery and contract management.
About the Role
You will assist with the development and delivery of infrastructure engineering projects, preparing designs, project plans, cost estimates, engineering specifications and tender documentation.
You will work across both operational and capital works, undertaking site investigations, inspections and project reviews, while providing practical engineering advice and recommendations to support quality project outcomes.
Key Responsibilities:
 - Assist with the planning, design and delivery of infrastructure projects.
 - Conduct site investigations and inspections and provide recommendations to address infrastructure issues.
 - Prepare project plans, engineering designs, specifications, cost estimates and tender documentation.
 - Monitor project works to ensure compliance with approved scope, specifications and objectives.
 - Support contract management and project administration.
 - Prepare reports, correspondence, grant submissions and other project documentation.
 - Assist with environmental assessments and obtaining relevant project approvals.
 - Provide professional and responsive service to internal stakeholders, contractors and the community.
 - Identify opportunities to improve project delivery, operational efficiency and service outcomes.
 - Promote Council’s work health and safety, risk management and environmental responsibilities.
 - Provide informed engineering recommendations based on project investigations and technical information.
About you
To be successful in this position, you will ideally have the following:
 - Currently undertaking, or recently completed, a tertiary qualification in Civil Engineering, or Project Management
 - Demonstrated project and time management skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and meet deadlines.
 - Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel and Outlook, as well as relevant project management, database and design/drafting software such as AutoCAD.
 - A current Class C Driver Licence.
What’s on offer
We are offering a remuneration between $79,533 to $91,463 per annum plus Super.
The City of Canada Bay also offers excellent employee benefits which include:
 - A range of flexible work arrangements including hybrid work from home arrangements
 - A supportive, energetic, and passionate team
 - Significant leave benefits (sick/personal leave, health and wellbeing leave, access to Long Service leave after 5 years)
 - Continuous training, support, and leadership development
 - Health and Wellbeing programs (Yoga classes, Fitness Passport, Flu vaccinations, Skin Cancer Checks)
 - And much, much more!
Want to know more?
Further information regarding the requirements of this role can be found in the attached Position Description, alternatively for a confidential discussion please contact Vincenzo Camuglia, Coordinator, Infrastructure Design on 02 9911 6287 or email Vincenzo.Camuglia@canadabay.nsw.gov.au 
How to apply
Candidates MUST apply online. Applications close 11:30pm, Thursday 22 October 2026 and will not be accepted through any other medium.
If you have any accessibility requirements, please feel free to contact Grace Aberin on 02 9121 0238  or email  grace.aberin@canadabay.nsw.gov.au   to discuss.
The City of Canada Bay Council is a Child Safe Organisation that recognises and advocates for the rights of Children and Young People and are committed to a Safe Workplace.
The City of Canada Bay Council is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer committed to maintaining, growing and supporting a diverse, respectful, collaborative & inclusive workplace. We welcome and encourage applications from diverse community groups and ages including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, LGBTIQA+, people with disabilities, and other diversity groups.

candidates.content_text:
GRADUATE / JUNIOR ESTIMATOR – COMMERCIAL CONSTRUCTION
Cairns, QLD | Full-Time | Graduate / Entry Level
WIP Construction is looking for a motivated Graduate or Junior Estimator to join our Cairns-based team. This is an office-based position located in Cairns, Queensland. Applicants must be based in Cairns or willing to relocate.
This is an opportunity for someone who wants to build a career in commercial construction estimating. You don't need previous experience as an Estimator, we're more interested in finding someone with the right aptitude, attitude and genuine desire to learn.
You may be a recent graduate, currently studying, or at the beginning of your construction career and looking for an opportunity to develop practical, hands-on experience within an established commercial construction company.
The Role
Working alongside our experienced estimating and project team, you'll learn how commercial construction projects are priced, tendered and ultimately delivered.
As your experience develops, you'll be involved in:
- Reviewing construction drawings, specifications and tender documentation
- Assisting with quantity take-offs and pricing
- Preparing and issuing subcontractor and supplier enquiries
- Reviewing and comparing quotations
- Assisting with tender submissions
- Understanding project scope, methodology and construction requirements
- Building relationships with subcontractors and suppliers
- Working with our project delivery team to understand how estimates translate into live projects
- Developing your knowledge of commercial construction costs, trades and procurement
We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. We'll teach you.
What we do expect is that you genuinely want to learn.
We're looking for someone who is curious, switched-on and interested in understanding how and why things are built and what they cost.
You may be studying or have recently completed a qualification in:
- Construction Management
- Quantity Surveying
- Civil Engineering
- Building & Construction
- Project Management
- Engineering
- Or another relevant construction-related discipline
We're also open to applicants from other backgrounds who can demonstrate strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in pursuing a career in construction estimating.
Previous estimating experience is not required.
More important to us is someone who:
- Has strong numerical and analytical skills
- Has excellent attention to detail
- Can read information carefully and ask questions when something doesn't make sense
- Is organised and able to manage competing priorities
- Communicates confidently and professionally
- Takes ownership of their work
- Has a genuine interest in building a long-term career in commercial construction
WIP Construction is an established Cairns-based commercial construction company delivering projects throughout Cairns and Far North Queensland.
You'll be joining a team where you'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced construction professionals and gain exposure to real commercial projects from tender through to delivery.
This isn't a graduate role where you'll spend months watching from the sidelines.
You'll be given real work, real responsibility and plenty of support while you develop your skills.
For the right person, there is significant opportunity to grow within the business and develop into an experienced Estimator.
If you're motivated, good with numbers, interested in construction and looking for somewhere to start your career, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, what you're currently studying or have completed, and why estimating and commercial construction interests you.

If our values resonate with you, please submit an application for the position. If you're not sure that you meet 100% of the selection criteria, that's okay, we would still like to hear from you and potentially discuss how your skills could be utilised at Fulton Hogan.

Site / Project Engineer - Civil & Concrete
Oakleigh Civil - South Australia
Join a growing South Australian civil construction company and build your career across project engineering, construction delivery, estimating and commercial management. 
About Oakleigh Civil 
Oakleigh Civil is a South Australian civil construction company specialising in civil infrastructure and structural concrete projects. Our capabilities include formwork, reinforcement, concrete placement and excavation. 
We work with on major infrastructure projects across metropolitan and regional South Australia, as well as interstate. 
Our work spans water infrastructure, defence, renewable energy, roads, mining and electrical infrastructure. 
Our experienced team takes a practical approach to delivering projects safely and to a very high standard. We value strong client relationships and take pride in being a contractor our clients can rely on.
About the role 
We are seeking a motivated Site / Project Engineer with at least three years’ construction experience to join our growing team. 
Working closely with the Construction Manager, company management, site supervisors and clients, you will help plan, coordinate and deliver projects from tender stage through to completion.  
The role combines site-based project management, estimating and commercial responsibilities. Unlike a traditional site engineering role, you will have exposure to the full project lifecycle, including estimating, procurement, construction delivery, cost control, variations, progress claims and project close-out. 
The successful candidate will be expected to take ownership of assigned projects, identify issues early and work with the project team to develop practical solutions. 
This position suits someone who is looking to broaden their capabilities, take greater responsibility and develop their career within a growing civil construction business.
Key responsibilities 
- Plan and coordinate construction activities with site supervisors to meet project requirements and construction programs. 
- Take ownership of allocated projects from planning through to completion. 
- Maintain regular communication with clients regarding project progress, upcoming works and any issues requiring resolution. 
- Review drawings, specifications and scope documents, identify issues, discrepancies, risks and constructability issues. 
- Assist with estimating, quantity take-offs, quotations and tender submissions. 
- Prepare and maintain project schedules, budgets, forecasts and progress reports. 
- Monitor project costs, cost-to-complete and forecasts. 
- Prepare and track project costs, variations and progress claims. 
- Coordinate procurement of materials, subcontractors and suppliers in accordance with project requirements and programs. 
- Coordinate project quality requirements, including ITP’s, inspections, testing, NCR’s and handover documentation. 
- Maintain accurate project documentation, registers, correspondence and records. 
- Support site safety requirements and work with supervisors to ensure works are planned and delivered safely. 
- Provide practical engineering and constructability advice to site teams. 
- Build and maintain effective relationships with clients, contractors and suppliers. 
About you 
- A degree in Civil Engineering or a relevant engineering discipline. 
- At least three years’ experience as a Site or Project Engineer in construction. 
- Experience in civil infrastructure or structural concrete works; formwork, reinforcement and concrete placement experience will be highly regarded. 
- Ability to interpret construction drawings, specifications and technical requirements. 
- Understanding of construction programming, project cost control, quality assurance and WHS requirements. 
- Strong organisation, communication and problem-solving skills. 
- Experience with variations, progress claims and project documentation. 
- Ability to manage competing priorities across multiple projects. 
- A practical approach, initiative and willingness to work closely with site supervisors and site crews. 
- Ability to identify problems early and take ownership of finding practical solutions. 
- Willingness and ability to work away from home when required. 
- A genuine desire to develop your skills and progress your career within a growing construction business. 
Why Join Oakleigh Civil?
- Varied projects: Work on civil infrastructure and structural concrete projects in metropolitan and regional South Australia, as well as interstate. 
- Broader experience: Gain exposure to the full project lifecycle, including estimating, procurement, construction, commercial management and project close out. 
- Direct involvement: Work closely with Construction Manager, company management and experienced site teams with the opportunity to influence how projects are delivered. 
- Career development: Build your capabilities across project management, estimating and commercial management, with genuine pathway to increase responsibility as the company grows. 
- Make a Contribution: Bring your ideas and help improve the way we work that supports Oakleigh Civil’s continued growth. 
Apply now 
If you’re looking to take the next step in your engineering career with Oakleigh Civil, apply through SEEK with your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience.

- Strong numeracy and analytical skills with meticulous attention to detail
- Confident in Microsoft Excel and comfortable working with spreadsheets and rate databases
- Ability to read and interpret construction, landscape and civil drawings
- A sound understanding of construction processes; exposure to paving, concrete, landscaping or civil works is a strong advantage
- Clear written and verbal communication and the ability to work as part of a small, hands-on team
- Capacity to manage several tenders at once and meet submission deadlines
- A keen interest in developing specialist estimating expertise and growing with the business
- Preferred: experience with take-off or estimating software, or exposure to tender and subcontract processes
What we offer
At Civilworks Australia Group you will learn estimating directly from the people who price, win and deliver the work. We are a growing specialist business, which means real responsibility early, direct exposure to clients and projects, and a clear path from junior to senior estimating as the business expands. We offer a supportive, collaborative workplace where your contribution is visible and valued, and where we invest in your professional development.
About us
Civilworks Australia Group is a Sydney-based paving and concrete specialist delivering high-quality public domain, commercial and residential works. We work with builders, head contractors and councils across NSW and are known for the quality of our paving and the reliability of our delivery. Our team is built on integrity, workmanship and strong relationships with our clients and suppliers.
Apply now
If you are detail-oriented, enjoy working with drawings and numbers, and want to build a career in specialist estimating, we would like to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a short cover letter outlining your interest in the role to sales@civilworksaus.com.au

About us
HHC Engineers is a growing engineering consultancy specialising in Structural, Civil and Post-Tension design. We deliver innovative and practical engineering solutions across a wide range of residential, commercial, industrial and high-rise projects along the East Coast of Australia. At HHC, we believe in collaboration, quality and continuous improvement, creating an environment where our people can learn, grow and build rewarding careers.
Benefits
- Career growth and professional development opportunities
- Work on a variety of projects
- Supportive and collaborative team environment
- Convenient location with easy access
 Qualifications & experience
- Completion of a four-year Civil Engineering qualification accredited by Engineers Australia, or equivalent
- Eligible for membership of Engineers Australia (M.I.E.Aust)
- 2–3 years’ experience in Site Engineering and Construction in Australia
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills
- Excellent attention to detail and organisational skills
- Proactive approach and commitment to professional development
- Australian working rights
- NSW Construction White Card
- Full Australian Driver’s Licence
Tasks & responsibilities
- Attend and conduct site inspections and structural investigations
- Prepare site inspection and engineering reports
- Assist with structural analysis, design and engineering calculations
- Apply engineering principles and technical methods to civil and structural projects
- Provide technical support to Senior Engineers and Management
- Assist with engineering tasks from investigation through to reporting and design
- Liaise with clients, contractors and other project stakeholders
- Manage multiple projects, assigned tasks and project deadlines
- Review and check technical work where required
- Maintain strong client relationships and deliver a high level of client service
- Contribute to a positive and collaborative team environment
- Software skills include: Microsoft Office, INDUCTA (RCB, SLB, RCC, FTG), RAPT & TEDDS

candidates.content_text:
Full Time, Permanent (76 hours per fortnight over 9 days) | $94,558 per annum plus 12% superannuation  
Country living and city convenience come together in the Lockyer Valley, serving as the perfect opportunity to pursue your career in a rural location.
Plating up an array of career opportunities, the Lockyer Valley is a leisurely one hour's drive from Australia's third largest city and home to affordable land prices with easy access to logistic hubs. Right on the doorstep of Brisbane, the region has some of the richest most productive agricultural land on earth and is home to more than 45,000 people.
The Lockyer Valley isn't just a great destination for exciting career opportunities, but also for leisure and lifestyle The region is perfect location to secure that sought-after work-life balance with immersive community experiences.
Lockyer Valley Regional Council is currently seeking applications from dynamic, innovative and highly experienced individuals to fill the position of Asset Engineer within our Infrastructure Planning team. This is a fantastic opportunity for the right person who has the required qualifications, experience and desire to undertake a challenging but fulfilling role in a values-driven organisation.
Eligibility Requirements
Applicants must have the legal right to work in Australia and hold a current drivers licence. Successful applicants will also be required to undertake pre-employment screening which will include a medical assessment, drug screen, and a criminal history check. 
To Apply
Please refer to Council’s website to view the information package which contains instructions on how to make an application. Applicants must submit a cover letter, resume and key selection criteria responses to Council. The key selection criteria questions which require responses can be found within the position description document of the information pack.
Applications for this position close at 5:00 pm (AEST) on Monday 26 October 2026.
For additional enquiries regarding this advertisement please contact Council's Organisational Development team on (07) 5466 3555.
LVRC IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER
